title: Explained | World's Water Crisis | FULL EPISODE | Netflix
speaker: Netflix
zh: 【Netflix】解釋 |世界水危機|完整影集 | Netflix（精選雙語跟讀教材）

cues.text: Turn on a faucet and clean water rushes out, as much as we want, anytime we want.
cues.en: Turn on a faucet and clean water rushes out, as much as we want, anytime we want.
cues.zh: 開啟水龍頭，乾淨的水就會源源不絕地流出來，想喝多少就喝多少。

cues.text: It's easy to forget that the quest for this has been one of the defining struggles of human history.
cues.en: It's easy to forget that the quest for this has been one of the defining struggles of human history.
cues.zh: 人們很容易忘記，對這一目標的追求一直是人類歷史上決定性的鬥爭之一。

cues.text: Civilizations that harnessed water, thrived.
cues.en: Civilizations that harnessed water, thrived.
cues.zh: 利用水的文明蓬勃發展。

cues.text: The ones that failed... fell.
cues.en: The ones that failed... fell.
cues.zh: 那些失敗的……倒下了。

cues.text: Today, seven in ten people on Earth can count on having running water in their homes.
cues.en: Today, seven in ten people on Earth can count on having running water in their homes.
cues.zh: 如今，地球上十分之七的人可以在家中使用自來水。

cues.text: The water flows from the risers to connecting mains, and finally through service connections into each building on the street.
cues.en: The water flows from the risers to connecting mains, and finally through service connections into each building on the street.
cues.zh: 水從立管流向連線的總管，最後透過服務連線流入街道上的每棟建築物。

cues.text: At least, so they think.
cues.en: At least, so they think.
cues.zh: 至少，他們是這麼認為的。

cues.text: Cape Town. It could become the first major city in the world to run out of water.
cues.en: Cape Town. It could become the first major city in the world to run out of water.
cues.zh: 開普敦。它可能成為世界上第一個缺水的主要城市。

cues.text: Cape Town, South Africa, is inching closer now to Day Zero.
cues.en: Cape Town, South Africa, is inching closer now to Day Zero.
cues.zh: 南非開普敦距離零日已經越來越近了。

cues.text: Just 92 days away from having to shut off most water taps
cues.en: Just 92 days away from having to shut off most water taps
cues.zh: 只需 92 天即可關閉大部分水龍頭

cues.text: because of a severe drought.
cues.en: because of a severe drought.
cues.zh: 因為嚴重的乾旱。

cues.text: Cape Town is the first major city in the world to plan to indefinitely shut off its water supply.
cues.en: Cape Town is the first major city in the world to plan to indefinitely shut off its water supply.
cues.zh: 開普敦是世界上第一個計劃無限期關閉供水的主要城市。

cues.text: Four million people would stop getting running water.
cues.en: Four million people would stop getting running water.
cues.zh: 四百萬人將無法獲得自來水。

cues.text: They'd get water rations, and they'd need to line up at city water stations to get it.
cues.en: They'd get water rations, and they'd need to line up at city water stations to get it.
cues.zh: 他們會得到配給的水，並且需要在城市供水站排隊才能得到。

cues.text: And it's not just Cape Town.
cues.en: And it's not just Cape Town.
cues.zh: 不僅僅是開普敦。

cues.text: São Paulo, Melbourne, Jakarta, London, Beijing, Istanbul, Tokyo, Bangalore,
cues.en: São Paulo, Melbourne, Jakarta, London, Beijing, Istanbul, Tokyo, Bangalore,
cues.zh: 聖保羅、墨爾本、雅加達、倫敦、北京、伊斯坦堡、東京、班加羅爾、

cues.text: Barcelona and Mexico City will all face their own Day Zero in the next few decades,
cues.en: Barcelona and Mexico City will all face their own Day Zero in the next few decades,
cues.zh: 巴塞隆納和墨西哥城都將在未來幾十年內面臨自己的“零日”，

cues.text: unless their water use radically changes.
cues.en: unless their water use radically changes.
cues.zh: 除非他們的用水量發生根本性的改變。

cues.text: There are perceptions that it is there in bountiful amounts and everyone has access to it because you can turn a tap,
cues.en: There are perceptions that it is there in bountiful amounts and everyone has access to it because you can turn a tap,
cues.zh: 有人認為它的數量非常豐富，每個人都可以使用它，因為你可以轉動水龍頭，

cues.text: and that's a big problem.
cues.en: and that's a big problem.
cues.zh: 這是一個大問題。

cues.text: In fact, by 2040 most of the world won't have enough water to meet demand year-round.
cues.en: In fact, by 2040 most of the world won't have enough water to meet demand year-round.
cues.zh: 事實上，到 2040 年，世界大部分地區將沒有足夠的水來滿足全年需求。

cues.text: We're facing a global water crisis and it's getting worse.
cues.en: We're facing a global water crisis and it's getting worse.
cues.zh: 我們正面臨全球水危機，而且情況變得更加嚴重。

cues.text: We're at a real inflection point where, if we're not careful, we may actually get out ahead of our ability to manage it.
cues.en: We're at a real inflection point where, if we're not careful, we may actually get out ahead of our ability to manage it.
cues.zh: 我們正處於一個真正的轉折點，如果我們不小心，我們實際上可能會超出我們的管理能力。

cues.text: There's no substitute for water.
cues.en: There's no substitute for water.
cues.zh: 水是無可取代的。

cues.text: Each of us will die in just a few days without it.
cues.en: Each of us will die in just a few days without it.
cues.zh: 如果沒有它，我們每個人都會在幾天之內死去。

cues.text: How have we built a world where we don't have enough of its most valuable resource?
cues.en: How have we built a world where we don't have enough of its most valuable resource?
cues.zh: 我們如何建立一個沒有足夠、最寶貴資源的世界？

cues.text: And as this crisis grows, what will the new world look like?
cues.en: And as this crisis grows, what will the new world look like?
cues.zh: 隨著這場危機的加劇，新世界會是什麼樣子？

cues.text: Waterways, built by the people to free the land of the tyranny of nature.
cues.en: Waterways, built by the people to free the land of the tyranny of nature.
cues.zh: 水道是人們為了將土地從大自然的暴虐中解放出來而建造的。

cues.text: For some investors, what they see in this glass is liquid gold.
cues.en: For some investors, what they see in this glass is liquid gold.
cues.zh: 對一些投資者來說，他們在這個玻璃杯中看到的是液態黃金。

cues.text: Clean water. Now.
cues.en: Clean water. Now.
cues.zh: 乾淨的水。現在。

cues.text: In defense of water. Water becomes a commodity.
cues.en: In defense of water. Water becomes a commodity.
cues.zh: 保衛水源。水成為一種商品。

cues.text: It takes on new value.
cues.en: It takes on new value.
cues.zh: 它呈現出新的價值。

cues.text: People claim it, haul it, treasure it.
cues.en: People claim it, haul it, treasure it.
cues.zh: 人們認領它、拖曳它、珍惜它。

cues.text: Dare we take our water supply for granted as we do the air we breathe?
cues.en: Dare we take our water supply for granted as we do the air we breathe?
cues.zh: 我們敢把水的供應視為理所當然，就像我們呼吸的空氣一樣嗎？

cues.text: Earth is the blue planet.
cues.en: Earth is the blue planet.
cues.zh: 地球是藍色的星球。

cues.text: There's no shortage of water. We have 326 million trillion gallons of it.
cues.en: There's no shortage of water. We have 326 million trillion gallons of it.
cues.zh: 不缺水。我們有 3.26 億萬億加侖。

cues.text: Always have, always will.
cues.en: Always have, always will.
cues.zh: 一直有，也永遠會。

cues.text: Water may freeze into ice or evaporate into air, but it doesn't leave our planet.
cues.en: Water may freeze into ice or evaporate into air, but it doesn't leave our planet.
cues.zh: 水可能會凍結成冰或蒸發到空氣中，但它不會離開我們的星球。

cues.text: If you sucked up all the water on Earth, it would fit into this sphere.
cues.en: If you sucked up all the water on Earth, it would fit into this sphere.
cues.zh: 如果你吸乾地球上所有的水，它就會適合這個球體。

cues.text: But 97% of it is salty and 2% is trapped in ice at the poles,
cues.en: But 97% of it is salty and 2% is trapped in ice at the poles,
cues.zh: 但其中 97% 是鹹的，2% 被困在兩極的冰中，

cues.text: so all of humankind relies on just 1% of that water to survive.
cues.en: so all of humankind relies on just 1% of that water to survive.
cues.zh: 因此全人類僅依靠 1% 的水生存。

cues.text: When people talk about running out of water, what they really mean is,
cues.en: When people talk about running out of water, what they really mean is,
cues.zh: 當人們談論缺水時，他們真正的意思是，

cues.text: do they have access to that very small percentage?
cues.en: do they have access to that very small percentage?
cues.zh: 他們能接觸到那麼小的比例嗎？

cues.text: And the answer depends a lot on where you live.
cues.en: And the answer depends a lot on where you live.
cues.zh: 答案很大程度取決於你住在哪裡。

cues.text: Kuwait is one of the poorest countries in terms of water per capita,
cues.en: Kuwait is one of the poorest countries in terms of water per capita,
cues.zh: 科威特是人均水資源最貧窮的國家之一

cues.text: and Canada, one of the richest, doesn't have twice as much or even ten times as much. It has 10,000 times as much.
cues.en: and Canada, one of the richest, doesn't have twice as much or even ten times as much. It has 10,000 times as much.
cues.zh: 而加拿大，作為最富有的國家之一，卻沒有兩倍甚至十倍的財富。它的數量是原來的一萬倍。

cues.text: But it also matters where the water is.
cues.en: But it also matters where the water is.
cues.zh: 但水在哪裡也很重要。

cues.text: That 1% of Earth's water that we all rely on, most of it is underground and really difficult and expensive to get to,
cues.en: That 1% of Earth's water that we all rely on, most of it is underground and really difficult and expensive to get to,
cues.zh: 我們所依賴的地球水的 1%，其中大部分位於地下，取得起來非常困難且昂貴，

cues.text: so humans have mostly settled close to surface water, like rivers and lakes.
cues.en: so humans have mostly settled close to surface water, like rivers and lakes.
cues.zh: 因此，人類大多定居在靠近地表水的地方，例如河流和湖泊。

cues.text: Around 90% of the world's population lives less than ten kilometers from a freshwater source.
cues.en: Around 90% of the world's population lives less than ten kilometers from a freshwater source.
cues.zh: 世界上大約 90% 的人口生活在距離淡水源不到 10 公里的地方。

cues.text: Hundreds of years ago, when the Aztecs settled on what is now Mexico City,
cues.en: Hundreds of years ago, when the Aztecs settled on what is now Mexico City,
cues.zh: 數百年前，當阿茲特克人定居在現在的墨西哥城時，

cues.text: they saw a giant lake.
cues.en: they saw a giant lake.
cues.zh: 他們看到了一個巨大的湖。

cues.text: These are the last remnants of the canals they made.
cues.en: These are the last remnants of the canals they made.
cues.zh: 這是他們修建的運河的最後遺跡。

cues.text: When the Spanish came in the 16th century, one soldier marveled at the Aztec city rising from the water
cues.en: When the Spanish came in the 16th century, one soldier marveled at the Aztec city rising from the water
cues.zh: 16 世紀西班牙人到來時，一名士兵驚嘆於阿茲特克城從水中升起

cues.text: that seemed like an enchanted vision.
cues.en: that seemed like an enchanted vision.
cues.zh: 這看起來像是一個令人著迷的景象。

cues.text: But then the Spanish started draining the lake, and over the next few centuries that space was filled by people.
cues.en: But then the Spanish started draining the lake, and over the next few centuries that space was filled by people.
cues.zh: 但後來西班牙人開始排乾湖水，在接下來的幾個世紀裡，這個空間被人類填滿了。

cues.text: Like in most places, surface water in Mexico was treated as a public resource, key to development.
cues.en: Like in most places, surface water in Mexico was treated as a public resource, key to development.
cues.zh: 與大多數地方一樣，墨西哥的地表水被視為公共資源，是發展的關鍵。

cues.text: And since 1950, Mexico City's population has exploded.
cues.en: And since 1950, Mexico City's population has exploded.
cues.zh: 自 1950 年以來，墨西哥城的人口呈現爆炸性成長。

cues.text: It's now home to 22 million people.
cues.en: It's now home to 22 million people.
cues.zh: 它現在是 2200 萬人的家園。

cues.text: I would say some of the most important threats for Mexico City are related to water.
cues.en: I would say some of the most important threats for Mexico City are related to water.
cues.zh: 我想說墨西哥城面臨的一些最重要的威脅與水有關。

cues.text: Mexico City gets more rain than notoriously rainy London.
cues.en: Mexico City gets more rain than notoriously rainy London.
cues.zh: 墨西哥城的降雨量比出了名的多雨的倫敦還要多。

cues.text: But the lakes that would have collected that water are long gone, so the city floods.
cues.en: But the lakes that would have collected that water are long gone, so the city floods.
cues.zh: 但本來可以收集這些水的湖泊早已消失，所以城市發生了洪水。

cues.text: But they still need to pipe in most of their water from other parts of Mexico.
cues.en: But they still need to pipe in most of their water from other parts of Mexico.
cues.zh: 但他們仍然需要從墨西哥其他地區輸送大部分水。

cues.text: Or they pump it from underground.
cues.en: Or they pump it from underground.
cues.zh: 或者他們從地下抽水。

cues.text: We've gotten a lot better at accessing groundwater.
cues.en: We've gotten a lot better at accessing groundwater.
cues.zh: 我們在獲取地下水方面已經取得了很大進展。

cues.text: But there's a catch.
cues.en: But there's a catch.
cues.zh: 但有一個問題。

cues.text: Those water deposits, called aquifers, have accumulated over millennia
cues.en: Those water deposits, called aquifers, have accumulated over millennia
cues.zh: 這些水沉積物，稱為含水層，已經累積了數千年

cues.text: and they'll take millennia to fill back up.
cues.en: and they'll take millennia to fill back up.
cues.zh: 他們需要幾千年的時間才能填滿。

cues.text: Groundwater is sort of like the savings account, which it's fine to draw on sometimes, especially when you have a drought.
cues.en: Groundwater is sort of like the savings account, which it's fine to draw on sometimes, especially when you have a drought.
cues.zh: 地下水有點像儲蓄帳戶，有時可以使用，尤其是在乾旱的時候。

cues.text: That's not what Mexico City's been doing.
cues.en: That's not what Mexico City's been doing.
cues.zh: 這不是墨西哥城一直在做的事情。

cues.text: We take out from the local aquifer around 50% of our water supply.
cues.en: We take out from the local aquifer around 50% of our water supply.
cues.zh: 我們大約 50% 的供水來自當地含水層。

cues.text: That means that probably we'll lose half of our supply of water
cues.en: That means that probably we'll lose half of our supply of water
cues.zh: 這意味著我們可能會失去一半的水供應

cues.text: in the next 30-50 years.
cues.en: in the next 30-50 years.

cues.text: Sucking up that groundwater has another side effect.
cues.en: Sucking up that groundwater has another side effect.
cues.zh: 抽吸地下水還有另一個副作用。

cues.text: It compresses the soil.
cues.en: It compresses the soil.
cues.zh: 它壓縮土壤。

cues.text: Mexico City is literally sinking.
cues.en: Mexico City is literally sinking.
cues.zh: 墨西哥城實際上正在下沉。

cues.text: In some places, as much as nine inches a year.
cues.en: In some places, as much as nine inches a year.
cues.zh: 在某些地方，每年多達九英寸。

cues.text: NASA satellite data shows aquifers in northern India decreasing by 29 trillion gallons in just a decade.
cues.en: NASA satellite data shows aquifers in northern India decreasing by 29 trillion gallons in just a decade.
cues.zh: NASA 衛星資料顯示，印度北部的含水層在短短十年內減少了 29 兆加侖。

cues.text: There are simply more people on Earth consuming more water.
cues.en: There are simply more people on Earth consuming more water.
cues.zh: 地球上有更多的人消耗更多的水。

cues.text: This century, water consumption has increased sevenfold.
cues.en: This century, water consumption has increased sevenfold.
cues.zh: 本世紀，用水量增加了七倍。

cues.text: And the rain and snow that we count on to water crops and refill lakes and rivers
cues.en: And the rain and snow that we count on to water crops and refill lakes and rivers
cues.zh: 我們依靠雨和雪來澆灌農作物並補充湖泊和河流

cues.text: is getting less reliable.
cues.en: is getting less reliable.
cues.zh: 越來越不可靠。

cues.text: Climate change is making available water much more erratic.
cues.en: Climate change is making available water much more erratic.
cues.zh: 氣候變遷使可用水變得更加不穩定。

cues.text: We're seeing areas around the world that are experiencing much more extended dry periods.
cues.en: We're seeing areas around the world that are experiencing much more extended dry periods.
cues.zh: 我們看到世界各地的一些地區正在經歷更長的乾旱期。

cues.text: But the problem isn't just that there's more people on Earth using water,
cues.en: But the problem isn't just that there's more people on Earth using water,
cues.zh: 但問題不僅僅是地球上有更多的人使用水，

cues.text: it's how we're using water.
cues.en: it's how we're using water.
cues.zh: 這就是我們用水的方式。

cues.text: Humans need to drink almost a gallon of water per day.
cues.en: Humans need to drink almost a gallon of water per day.
cues.zh: 人類每天需要喝幾乎一加侖的水。

cues.text: Brushing your teeth, washing your hands typically uses about a gallon.
cues.en: Brushing your teeth, washing your hands typically uses about a gallon.
cues.zh: 刷牙、洗手通常使用約一加侖。

cues.text: There goes three gallons.
cues.en: There goes three gallons.
cues.zh: 三加侖了。

cues.text: But the drinking, washing and toilet flushing of every person on Earth only accounts for 8% of our freshwater use each year.
cues.en: But the drinking, washing and toilet flushing of every person on Earth only accounts for 8% of our freshwater use each year.
cues.zh: 但地球上每個人的飲用、洗滌和沖洗馬桶僅佔我們每年淡水使用量的 8%。

cues.text: Most of the water goes to agriculture and industry, and into the food and products we use.
cues.en: Most of the water goes to agriculture and industry, and into the food and products we use.
cues.zh: 大部分水都流向農業和工業，以及我們使用的食品和產品。

cues.text: Let's take a bottle of Coca-Cola.
cues.en: Let's take a bottle of Coca-Cola.
cues.zh: 我們來一瓶可口可樂。

cues.text: 98% of the water in that bottle is not what you see in that bottle.
cues.en: 98% of the water in that bottle is not what you see in that bottle.
cues.zh: 那個瓶子裡 98% 的水不是你在那個瓶子裡看到的。

cues.text: 98% of the water is actually embedded in all the ingredients that were grown
cues.en: 98% of the water is actually embedded in all the ingredients that were grown
cues.zh: 98% 的水實際上嵌入了所有種植的成分中

cues.text: to make that bottle of Coca-Cola.
cues.en: to make that bottle of Coca-Cola.
cues.zh: 製作那瓶可口可樂

cues.text: 74 liters of water goes into every glass of beer.
cues.en: 74 liters of water goes into every glass of beer.
cues.zh: 每杯啤酒含有 74 公升水。

cues.text: A cup of coffee? 130 liters.
cues.en: A cup of coffee? 130 liters.
cues.zh: 一杯咖啡？ 130 公升。

cues.text: Each of your cotton shirts - 2,500 liters.
cues.en: Each of your cotton shirts - 2,500 liters.
cues.zh: 每件棉質襯衫 - 2,500 公升。

cues.text: But nothing has as much embedded water as meat.
cues.en: But nothing has as much embedded water as meat.
cues.zh: 但沒有什麼比肉含有更多的水分了。

cues.text: Alfalfa is a common ingredient in cattle feed, and growing a kilogram of it takes 510 liters of water.
cues.en: Alfalfa is a common ingredient in cattle feed, and growing a kilogram of it takes 510 liters of water.
cues.zh: 苜蓿是牛飼料中的常見成分，種植一公斤苜蓿需要 510 公升水。

cues.text: An average cow consumes about 12 kilograms of feed a day.
cues.en: An average cow consumes about 12 kilograms of feed a day.
cues.zh: 平均一頭乳牛每天消耗約12公斤飼料。

cues.text: Divided up, just one quarter-pound hamburger takes around 1,650 liters of water to produce.
cues.en: Divided up, just one quarter-pound hamburger takes around 1,650 liters of water to produce.
cues.zh: 生產一個四分之一磅的漢堡需要大約 1,650 公升水。

cues.text: The world is eating more and more like Americans.
cues.en: The world is eating more and more like Americans.
cues.zh: 世界各地的飲食習慣越來越像美國人。

cues.text: Higher calorie diets with more meat.
cues.en: Higher calorie diets with more meat.
cues.zh: 高熱量飲食，多吃肉。

cues.text: But everyone can't eat like Americans.
cues.en: But everyone can't eat like Americans.
cues.zh: 但不能每個人都像美國人一樣吃飯。

cues.text: There actually isn't enough water in the world.
cues.en: There actually isn't enough water in the world.
cues.zh: 事實上，世界上沒有足夠的水。

cues.text: Water doesn't abide by some of the basic rules of capitalism.
cues.en: Water doesn't abide by some of the basic rules of capitalism.

cues.text: How are you supposed to value an invaluable resource while ensuring everybody has it?
cues.en: How are you supposed to value an invaluable resource while ensuring everybody has it?
cues.zh: 您應該如何評估寶貴的資源，同時確保每個人都擁有它？

cues.text: When the price of water is raised, to fix pipes or encourage conservation,
cues.en: When the price of water is raised, to fix pipes or encourage conservation,
cues.zh: 當水價上漲時，為了修復管道或鼓勵節約用水，

cues.text: it has the greatest impact on the poor.
cues.en: it has the greatest impact on the poor.
cues.zh: 它對窮人的影響最大。

cues.text: Sydney water is pushing for a 15% hike over four years,
cues.en: Sydney water is pushing for a 15% hike over four years,
cues.zh: 雪梨水費力爭在四年內上漲 15%，

cues.text: putting more pressure on family budgets.
cues.en: putting more pressure on family budgets.
cues.zh: 給家庭預算帶來更大壓力。

cues.text: This drive for water conservation, water saving, is now a burden that poor people must carry.
cues.en: This drive for water conservation, water saving, is now a burden that poor people must carry.
cues.zh: 這種節約用水、節約用水的運動，現在成為貧窮人口必須承擔的負擔。

cues.text: Living on a fixed income, I cannot afford any of this.
cues.en: Living on a fixed income, I cannot afford any of this.
cues.zh: 靠固定收入過活，我負擔不起這些。

cues.text: It might be that we don't end up treating all water equally.
cues.en: It might be that we don't end up treating all water equally.
cues.zh: 也許我們最終並沒有平等地對待所有的水。

cues.text: We know that there is a certain percentage of water,
cues.en: We know that there is a certain percentage of water,
cues.zh: 我們知道水有一定的比例，

cues.text: it's around 60 liters per day per person, that is associated with human rights issues,
cues.en: it's around 60 liters per day per person, that is associated with human rights issues,
cues.zh: 每人每天約 60 公升，與人權問題有關，

cues.text: but above that, people should pay for water.
cues.en: but above that, people should pay for water.
cues.zh: 但除此之外，人們還應該為水付費。

cues.text: In 2017, Philadelphia started experimenting with tying water prices to income.
cues.en: In 2017, Philadelphia started experimenting with tying water prices to income.
cues.zh: 2017年，費城開始嘗試將水價與收入掛鉤。

cues.text: We need to price it in such a way that we protect basic human needs.
cues.en: We need to price it in such a way that we protect basic human needs.
cues.zh: 我們需要以保護人類基本需求的方式定價。

cues.text: The fact that we all need water makes this crisis exceptionally hard.
cues.en: The fact that we all need water makes this crisis exceptionally hard.
cues.zh: 我們都需要水這一事實使得這場危機異常艱難。

cues.text: But it can also inspire people to act in exceptional ways to solve it.
cues.en: But it can also inspire people to act in exceptional ways to solve it.
cues.zh: 但它也可以激勵人們以特殊的方式採取行動來解決這個問題。

cues.text: Cape Town's Day Zero was first scheduled for March 18.
cues.en: Cape Town's Day Zero was first scheduled for March 18.
cues.zh: 開普敦的「零日」原定於 3 月 18 日舉行。

cues.text: But then people started conserving.
cues.en: But then people started conserving.
cues.zh: 但後來人們開始節約。

cues.text: The water restrictions are clearly having some effect.
cues.en: The water restrictions are clearly having some effect.
cues.zh: 限水措施顯然產生了一些效果。

cues.text: Day Zero has been pushed back by a month.
cues.en: Day Zero has been pushed back by a month.
cues.zh: 「零日」已延後一個月。

cues.text: Cape Town announced it pushed back Day Zero until July 9th.
cues.en: Cape Town announced it pushed back Day Zero until July 9th.
cues.zh: 開普敦宣佈將「零日」推遲到 7 月 9 日。

cues.text: Authorities expect Day Zero, as it's been dubbed, to take place at the end of August instead of July.
cues.en: Authorities expect Day Zero, as it's been dubbed, to take place at the end of August instead of July.
cues.zh: 當局預計「零日」（即所謂的「零日」）將於八月底而不是七月發生。

cues.text: Now, that's since been pushed back to next year, thanks to extraordinary efforts of residents and authorities.
cues.en: Now, that's since been pushed back to next year, thanks to extraordinary efforts of residents and authorities.
cues.zh: 現在，由於居民和當局的非凡努力，這一目標已被推遲到明年。

cues.text: By early 2018, the city's water consumption was less than half what it had been just four years earlier,
cues.en: By early 2018, the city's water consumption was less than half what it had been just four years earlier,
cues.zh: 到 2018 年初，該市的用水量還不到四年前的一半，

cues.text: and the Day Zero countdown clock was paused indefinitely.
cues.en: and the Day Zero countdown clock was paused indefinitely.
cues.zh: 零日倒數被無限期暫停。

cues.text: Not enough action was taken until they started talking about Day Zero.
cues.en: Not enough action was taken until they started talking about Day Zero.
cues.zh: 在他們開始談論「零日」之前，並沒有採取足夠的行動。

cues.text: That really got people's attention.
cues.en: That really got people's attention.
cues.zh: 這確實引起了人們的注意。

cues.text: And it was remarkable, between the time that the city started to talk about Day Zero
cues.en: And it was remarkable, between the time that the city started to talk about Day Zero
cues.zh: 值得注意的是，在這座城市開始談論「零日」期間

cues.text: and, a month later, how much people cut back their water use.
cues.en: and, a month later, how much people cut back their water use.
cues.zh: 一個月後，有多少人減少了用水量。

cues.text: And it goes to show what we can do.
cues.en: And it goes to show what we can do.
cues.zh: 這表明我們可以做什麼。

cues.text: But Cape Town also got lucky.
cues.en: But Cape Town also got lucky.
cues.zh: 但開普敦也很幸運。

cues.text: It rained.
cues.en: It rained.
cues.zh: 下雨了。

cues.text: The trick is recognizing how valuable water is before there isn't enough of it,
cues.en: The trick is recognizing how valuable water is before there isn't enough of it,
cues.zh: 訣竅是在水不足之前認識到水的價值，

cues.text: and remembering that our fates are tied to what rushes out of our taps.
cues.en: and remembering that our fates are tied to what rushes out of our taps.
cues.zh: 並記住我們的命運與從水龍頭流出的水息息相關。

cues.text: Mexico City was founded within a lake.
cues.en: Mexico City was founded within a lake.
cues.zh: 墨西哥城建在一個湖中。

cues.text: But today our relation with water is very distant.
cues.en: But today our relation with water is very distant.
cues.zh: 但今天我們與水的關係卻非常遙遠。

cues.text: It's very important to recover our historical consciousness with water.
cues.en: It's very important to recover our historical consciousness with water.
cues.zh: 用水來恢復我們的歷史意識是非常重要的。

cues.text: There are many actions individuals can take in order to save water,
cues.en: There are many actions individuals can take in order to save water,
cues.zh: 個人可以採取許多行動來節約用水，

cues.text: but also to be aware that water has a value.
cues.en: but also to be aware that water has a value.
cues.zh: 但也要意識到水是有價值的。
